outcome.answer: Internal representations of language models seem to correlate with human sentence effort in a layered way: early layers can model naturalistic reading-time difficulty, while later layers better estimate harder syntactic-ambiguity effort, though they still underestimate human cost [1]. More generally, human reading behavior is better explained by model features that capture meaningful information in LM representations, and by measures tied to surprisal or storage-like uncertainty over future context [2, 5].
